again: Fit like, back again? Sit yersel doon, ye're lettin the heat oot.
I thocht ye'd gone for good. Nae such luck, eh? Only teasin.

sunshine: Look at that, the granite's fairly sparkling the day. Dinna say I never tell ye anything.

again: A fresh pair of ears. I have run out of people to complain to about the bins.
You again. Fair enough, the kettle was getting lonely.
morning: Mornings in this house are mostly me looking for my other shoe.

again: Och, ye're back. Gran would have put the kettle on before ye reached the door.
Ye'll wear a groove in the step. Mind, I dinna mind.

gale: Listen to that wind off the sea. Fittie folk just nod at it, like an old neighbour.

again: Sit doon, sit doon, ye look like ye could dae wi a rowie.
Ye're back. I'd say I'm surprised, but ye've the look of a body that likes company.
morning: Mornings I'm no fit to speak till the tea has gone in. After that, mind, I'm unstoppable.

again: Ah, the file reopens. The paperwork has not moved, but it has had a good rest.
Ah, a returning visitor. Please sign the book. It is more for my morale than anything.
Oh, you again. Come in, the kettle works even if the radiator does not.
Someone to blame the washing up on. Perfect timing.
evening: It is gone nine and I am only now thinking about the essay due tomorrow. Tradition, really.

again: I was just telling the tide about you. It was not impressed.
Ah, it is you. Sit down, I have a story, and it gets better each time I tell it.

gale: Wind like this and I am glad to be indoors. I tell Mair it is wisdom. She says it is knees.

again: Duw, bach, Idris has been sulking at the window all week. Cheer him up.
Come in, come in. He will say he never missed you. He did.
You are back! Nain made more, and I am being very brave not eating the lot.
Are you staying? Keep an eye on the plate for me.
morning: Mornings Nain has the bakestone out and the whole house smells like Sunday, whatever day it is.

again: Sit, sit, bach. You are looking thin, and I say that to everyone.
Well, look who it is. The kettle will not be a minute.
Cariad, you came back. The cat has been waiting by the door, or so she says.
Good, a fresh opinion. I have knitted something and nobody here will admit to liking it.

winter: Winter in this cottage means wool, tea and not answering the door before ten.

again: Wipe your feet, dear, I mean it this time.
Oh, it is you. The shortbread has been watching the door too.

rain: Rain again. Never mind, the tea is better for it and so is the company.

again: Back, are you? Good. Clear nights make me chatty and nobody listens.
Ah, a visitor. Have a peer, but mind that eyepiece, it takes offence.
evening: Evening is my morning, really. The sky starts its day and so do I.

again: Mind how you go, my lover, and sit down before you fall down.
There you are. I was just saying to the cat that someone nice would turn up.
Oh good, a distraction. My revision timetable thanks you.
You are back. I have read the same page four times. Talk to me.
evening: Evening is when I do my best work, or at least when I do any.

again: Back in? Come on, the kettle is still warm. Well, warm-ish.
Catch yourself on, I was only thinking about you. Come in, sit down.
Ah, you are back. Pull up a chair, I will tell you the story again and it will be better.
Another visit, is it? You have the look of someone who likes a good yarn.
It is half three, love, and nobody has done their homework, so excuse the wee racket.
In out of that, now. The tea is stewed, but sure it is the thought that counts.
evening: Evenings here are tea, telly and the cat refusing to move off the best seat.

again: The ferns noticed your absence. They are very sensitive.
Ah, you return. Keep your coat on, the warm air will make you sleepy.

winter: Winter is the best time to be in here. Outside is grey, in here it is a different country.

again: I'm back. I mean, I never left. I am still recovering on this step.
You came back up? Brave. I'm told there's a lift somewhere. There isn't, is there.
Twice up the stairs. Not many do that, so I take it as a compliment.
Watch the rail, and watch your knees, they will let you know tomorrow.
evening: Evening is the best part of the job. The light comes on, and I pretend it was my idea.

again: Sit yourself down, bab, the kettle never went off.
Well, look what the cat dragged in. Only joking, the cat dragged in a sock.
morning: Mornings here start with tea, then more tea, then thinking about breakfast.

again: You are back! Sit, sit. The biscuits have been getting restless.
Ah, my friend. Come and sit. There is always room and always tea.
Oh, you again. Want to hear another word nobody else believes?
You came back! Gran says that means you like us.
You are back! My project is nearly done, and I need someone to be impressed.
Oh good, a visitor. Do you want to hear my presentation? It is mostly done.
Back, are you? Mind if I tell you about the delays on the old route? Everything was late.
Ah, a regular. Thirty years of that and I can spot one at fifty paces.

rain: Rain like this and I remember every wet day I drove. Slow, steamy, and nobody cheerful.

again: Well, come in, hen, and mind the bannocks.
Ach, ye're no lost, are ye? Sit doon a minute.
morning: I'm up before the first loaf. The oven doesna wait for anybody, and neither do I.

again: The oven's hot and my patience is hotter, hen. Only joking, mostly.
Come in, come in. Ye've the look of a body that needs a pie.
morning: First batch is just out. Come in before it's all gone, hen.

again: Come away in. I was just going for a dander, but sure it can wait.
Well now, look who it is. The tea's wet, as they say.
Quietly, please. Something has just landed and I do not want it spooked.
Ah, you. Sit, but stay still. Birds have long memories for bad manners.
morning: Early light is the best for watching. I am usually at this window before the kettle boils.

again: Ye'll catch yer death in that smirr. Come in.
Ah, it's yersel. The boy's out the back pretending he isna cold.

fog: Fog's sat on the loch the day. Ye canna see the far shore, and I like it that way.

again: Mind the glaur on yer boots, I've only just swept.
Ah, ye're back. Pull up a chair and tell me something I havena heard.

rain: Ach, there's the rain on the window again. At least it's no snow. Yet.

again: Do wipe your feet. The last lodger did not, and I am still bitter.
Oh, it is you. I trust you have not been punting. They always come back damp.
morning: Mornings I'm up for the post and the porridge. The lodgers are up for neither.

again: You are back. Good, I need someone who does not know what a lemma is.
Perfect timing. I am procrastinating beautifully.
evening: It is late and I am still on problem four. Tell me it is normal.

again: Pull up a chair, butt, I'm not going anywhere.
Alright, butt. Good to see a face that stops to listen.
Come here, cariad, and have a cwtch before you go.
Ah, you're back. The kettle's on, the cat's on the settee, all is well.
morning: Mornings I do the crossword and pretend I haven't got it wrong.

again: Sit down, mate, I'm just trying to find where my match ticket went.
Come in, come in. The telly is on but nobody is watching, as usual.

rain: Rain on a Saturday and Ffion still wants to play outside. I admire it, really.

again: Is it yourself, pet? You have the look of someone who left without saying goodbye.
Well, well. Come in, then. I'll count the spoons after.
Yes, I remember you. I never forget a face, family motto and all.
Ah, you've returned. I was just telling the dog about you. He didn't care.
Ye've the look of someone who could use a hot roll, hen.
Och, it's yersel. Sit doon, the canal's no going anywhere.

fog: Fog on the canal this morning. Ye could hear the boats before ye saw them.

again: Sit down before I put the kettle on without asking, love.
Ah, there you are. I was only after saying you'd be back.
Grand, grand. The tea is on and so is the match, so it's a good day.
You're a sight for sore eyes, or at least a sight.

rain: Rain again. Sure that's Cork for you. You get used to it, or you move to Spain.

again: You came back! Do you want to hear the tin whistle? Please say no, I'm only warming up.
Oh, hi. Dad says I'm improving. He's lying, but kindly.
You're gas, you are. Come in, the kettle's still warm.
Ah sure, the door was only open for you. Sit down.
Careful, there's wool on everything. You will leave covered in it.
Oh good, you're back. Feel this one, it's softer than yesterday's, I swear.

spring: Spring means shearing and sore arms, but the new fleece smells lovely.

again: You return. Good. A man likes an audience, particularly one who appreciates a fine staple.
Just in time. I have been grading since dawn and my eyes have turned to wool.
